Therefore the only biconditional that is not equivalent to the rest is number 5.

Let Bob’s three integer guesses be ordered  g₁ ≤ g₂ ≤ g₃.
After Bob guesses, the host reveals the coin counts (a,b,c) with a ≤ b ≤ c, then pairs them adversarially as (g₃→a , g₂→b , g₁→c).  Bob’s payoff is
 P = g₃·1[g₃≤a] + g₂·1[g₂≤b] + g₁                                       (1)
(the last term always pays because g₁ ≤ c).

All legal coin distributions are the seven of the form
(a,a+6,24−2a) for a = 0…6, and the five of the form
(24−2b, b, b+6) for b = 8…12.
Their smallest middle count is b_min = 6 (realised at (0,6,24)), and their smallest largest count is c_min = 12 (realised at (6,12,12)).  The smallest smallest count is a_min = 0.

To guarantee any coins from the middle box we must have g₂ ≤ 6.  Because g₁ ≤ g₂, this forces g₁ ≤ 6, so g₁ + g₂ ≤ 12.  The first term in (1) can contribute only if g₃ ≤ a_min = 0, i.e. only when g₃ = 0, which would reduce g₁ and g₂ as well; therefore we accept that the first term will be zero in the worst case.

Hence Bob’s maximum guaranteed payoff is at most 12 coins, attained if g₁ = g₂ = 6.  Taking g₃ = 6 as well gives the guess triple (6,6,6).  Against any legal distribution the numbers of boxes containing at least six coins is at least two, so Bob always receives 6 + 6 = 12 coins, and no strategy can force more.

Each coin is worth $1,000, so the minimum amount of money Bob can assure himself is 12×1,000 = 12,000.
Sort Bob’s guesses so that a≤b≤c.

1. Host’s counter–strategies
   • If a≥13: choose coin allocation (6,12,12).  Each count is <13, so all three guesses fail and Bob wins 0≤12.
   • If a≤12: choose allocation (0,6,24).  Assign 24-coin box to guess a, 6-coin box to the largest remaining guess that is ≤6 (if any), and 0-coin box to the remaining guess.
        – Bob is paid a from the 24-coin box (a≤12).
        – Any additional payment can only come from the 6-coin box, whose guess is ≤6.
        – Thus total payoff ≤12.
   Both allocations satisfy the game constraints (one pair differs by 6; at least one box has ≥2 coins).

Hence, for any triple of guesses the host can keep Bob’s winnings to at most 12 coins.  Conversely, if Bob guesses (12,12,12), every legal coin placement gives him at least one box with ≥12 coins, so he is guaranteed exactly 12 coins.

Therefore Bob’s optimal guaranteed gain is 12 coins, i.e. $12,000.

Among BayStars pitchers as of July 2023, the closest lower-numbered pitcher was Yutaro Ishida (#54) and the closest higher-numbered pitcher was Rowan Wick (#62). Hence, the pitchers immediately before and after the (misattributed) number are Ishida and Wick.
